name: Sons of the Invincible Mahrem

abilities.name: Sea Sickness
abilities.text: As these men are inexperienced sailors. Caught up in sea combat, they suffer various penalties.

abilities.name: Shield Screen
abilities.text: The unit raises their shields in a static defensive formation.

abilities.name: Frenzy
abilities.text: Improves a unit's attack capabilities for an extended period of time.

attributes.name: Expert Charge Defence
attributes.text: This unit’s melee attack and damage are increased against charging enemies.

attributes.name: Disciplined
attributes.text: This unit does not suffer a morale penalty when the general dies. It can also rally after routing more often.

attributes.name: Resistant to Fatigue
attributes.text: Fatigue has less of an effect on this unit.

attributes.name: Hide (forest)
attributes.text: This unit can hide in forests until enemy units get too close.

attributes.name: Scare (everyone)
attributes.text: This unit frightens all enemy units.

attributes.name: Immune to Fear
attributes.text: This unit is immune to the fear effects of scary units.

short: They kill at the command of the war god himself.
history: Prior to their conversion to Christianity, the people of Aksum practiced their own brand of polytheistic paganism within a system not dissimilar to that of the ancient Greeks. Within their pantheon, Mahrem, also known as Maher, was the god of war, and can be likened to the Greek Ares or the Roman Mars in that he is a representation of its barbarous, untamed, and ill-considered side - as opposed to planned strategy and tactics. As the son of Ishtar, the god of the morning star and the central Aksumite deity, Mahrem held an exalted position above many of the pantheon’s lesser gods. Aksum’s warrior king was even referred to as the "Son of Invincible Mahrem", indicating that not only was he considered a god by his people, but that he ruled over a society in which warfare was central.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
